description: Introduction and overview of the Brooklyn-class Cruiser: What this class is, its role in the fleet, and why it matters in naval history. The Brooklyn class — nine built (seven U.S., two Argentine) — were light cruisers armed with fifteen 6-inch/47 guns in five triple turrets, the heaviest light-cruiser broadside of the war. Brooklyns fought in the Mediterranean, Normandy, and the Pacific; Argentina's General Belgrano was sunk in the Falklands War. Baseline facts: U.S. WWII light cruiser; 9 built; fifteen 6-inch guns; Belgrano sunk 1982..
